questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-3 & \sqrt{3} \\ 1 & \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the coordinates of the point ${S}^{′}$, the image of $S(-4,\sqrt{3})$ under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of $S$ under the action of $T$, we first create a column-vector $x$ containing the coordinates of $S:$

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $x$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $Tx:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Tx & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & \sqrt{3} \\ 1 & \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-4 \\ \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}15 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The result, $Tx,$ contains the coordinates of ${S}^{′}.$ Therefore, ${S}^{′}(15,-1).$

questions.problem:
Consider the line $y=5x-2$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=5x-2$ passes through the points $A(0,-2)$ and $B(1,3)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $A$ and $B$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 8 & -15\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${A}^{′}(0,8)$ and ${B}^{′}(1,-15).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${A}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-8 & =\frac{-15-8}{1-0}(x-0) \\ y-8 & =-23x \\ 23x+y-8 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the line $y=-x-4$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T?$

First, notice that the line $y=-x-4$ passes through the points $W(0,-4)$ and $Z(1,-5)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $W$ and $Z$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -4 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -4 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 9 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${W}^{′}(8,0)$ and ${Z}^{′}(9,-3).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${W}^{′}$ and ${Z}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-0 & =\frac{-3-0}{9-8}(x-8) \\ y & =-3(x-8) \\ y & =-3x+24 \\ 3x+y-24 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the line $y=\frac{1}{3}x+1$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=15.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=\frac{1}{3}x+1$ passes through the points $A(0,1)$ and $B(3,2)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $A$ and $B$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 16 \\ -1 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${A}^{′}(2,-1)$ and ${B}^{′}(16,7).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${A}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y+1 & =\frac{7-(-1)}{16-2}(x-2) \\ y+1 & =\frac{8}{14}(x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y+1 & =\frac{4}{7}(x-2) \\ 7y+7 & =4x-8 \\ 4x-7y & =15\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that the line $y=x+1$ passes through the points $A(0,1)$ and $B(1,2)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $A$ and $B$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${A}^{′}(2,3)$ and ${B}^{′}(5,4).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${A}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-3 & =\frac{1}{3}(x-2) \\ 3y-9 & =x-2 \\ x-3y & =-7\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 5 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & -4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

To find the image of $U$ and $V$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 5 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${U}^{′}(-12,-3)$ and ${V}^{′}(5,-1).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${A}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-3) & =\frac{-1-(-3)}{5-(-12)}(x-(-12)) \\ y+3 & =\frac{2}{17}(x+12)\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $\mathbf T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are $P'(0,-2)$ and $Q'(-1,4).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through $P'$ and $Q'\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-2) & =\frac{4-(-2)}{-1-0}(x-0) \\ y+2 & =-6x \\ 6x+y+2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Image of a Line Given by an Equation in Standard Form
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the line $5x-y-3=0$ and linear transformation $\mathbf T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14055459/assets/3b0c64bc040716ca8ba42c78a229d1249ec7f80a3a4a584970863b20126c69db.png)

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $\mathbf T?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, let's find two points on the given line. Solving for $y,$ we get $y=5x-3,$ and substituting $x=0$ and $x=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0\, & \to \,y=5(0)-3=-3, \\ x=1\, & \to \,y=5(1)-3=2.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have two points on the line, $P(0,-3)$ and $Q(1,2).$

To find the images of $P$ and $Q$ under the action of $\mathbf T,$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of $P$ and $Q$ in its columns:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14055459/assets/a32e0386507fdc40cc713854dde4ec413c2dfbb4c49a6e758e8690344f08459a.png)

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $\mathbf T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ -6 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are $P'(-3,-6)$ and $Q'(-1,3).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through $P'$ and $Q'\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-6) & =\frac{3-(-6)}{-1-(-3)}(x-(-3)) \\ y+6 & =\frac{9}{2}(x+3) \\ 2y+12 & =9x+27 \\ 9x-2y+15 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
